questions.question: In which year did World War II end?
questions.explanation: The war in Europe ended in May 1945 and the war in the Pacific in September 1945.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington served as president from 1789 to 1797.

questions.question: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids of Giza?
questions.explanation: The Giza pyramids were built by ancient Egyptians as royal tombs, around 2600–2500 BC.

questions.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: The wall was opened on 9 November 1989, and Germany reunified in 1990.

questions.question: Which empire built the Colosseum in Rome?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum was completed under the Roman Empire in AD 80.

questions.question: In which year did the French Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: The Revolution began in 1789, famously with the storming of the Bastille on 14 July.

questions.question: Who was the first emperor of a unified China, founding the Qin dynasty?
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang unified China in 221 BC and took the title of first emperor.

questions.question: In which year was Magna Carta sealed by King John of England?
questions.explanation: Magna Carta was sealed at Runnymede in 1215, limiting the king's powers.

questions.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 15th century, high in the Peruvian Andes.

questions.question: The Treaty of Versailles formally ended which war?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919 and formally ended World War I with Germany.

questions.question: Who founded the Mongol Empire in 1206?
questions.explanation: Temüjin was proclaimed Genghis Khan in 1206 after uniting the Mongol tribes.

questions.question: Which ship carried the Pilgrims from England to America in 1620?
questions.explanation: The Mayflower landed at Cape Cod in November 1620, with about 100 passengers.

questions.question: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: It began in Britain in the 18th century, driven by textiles, coal and steam power.

questions.question: In which country did the Renaissance begin?
questions.explanation: The Renaissance began in 14th-century Italy, notably in Florence.

questions.question: Which Carthaginian general famously crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome?
questions.explanation: Hannibal made the crossing in 218 BC during the Second Punic War.

questions.question: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969, and Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the surface.

questions.question: The Hundred Years' War was fought mainly between which two kingdoms?
questions.explanation: It lasted from 1337 to 1453, with periods of truce, between England and France.

questions.question: In which year did the Cuban Missile Crisis take place?
questions.explanation: The crisis lasted thirteen days in October 1962 and brought the US and USSR close to nuclear war.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics and later won a second in Chemistry in 1911.

questions.question: The Rosetta Stone helped scholars decipher which writing system?
questions.explanation: Its text appears in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek, which let Champollion crack hieroglyphs in the 1820s.

questions.question: In which year is the fall of the Western Roman Empire traditionally dated?
questions.explanation: In 476 the last Western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed by Odoacer.

questions.question: In which year was the Battle of Hastings fought?
questions.explanation: William of Normandy defeated King Harold at Hastings in 1066.

questions.question: Who was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom for most of World War II?
questions.explanation: Churchill led the wartime government from May 1940 to July 1945.

questions.question: Whose expedition completed the first circumnavigation of the globe between 1519 and 1522?
questions.explanation: Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521. Juan Sebastián Elcano led the surviving ship home.

questions.question: Which empire was ruled by Suleiman the Magnificent?
questions.explanation: Suleiman ruled the Ottoman Empire from 1520 to 1566, at its height of power.

questions.question: In which year did the Titanic sink?
questions.explanation: The Titanic struck an iceberg and sank on 15 April 1912.

questions.question: Which Roman emperor ordered the construction of a wall across northern Britain in AD 122?
questions.explanation: Hadrian's Wall marked the northern frontier of Roman Britain.

questions.question: Who became the first person in space in 1961?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth in Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.
